name: quoin_corner
title: Alternating long and short stone blocks on the side studs of a wall's corner columns; use on cottages and town houses.
why: Stone corners in a contrasting color, long and short blocks alternating, on any house corner or door jamb; one of the clearest signs of a designed building.

name: wall_top_tie
title: A course of plates across the tops of the walls, over the corner joints, finished with tiles except a few studs to locate what goes on top.
why: A course of plates across the wall tops that overlaps every corner joint, then tiles that leave a few studs: what locks walls together and lets a floor or roof lift off. The cottage needs it.

name: lift_off_roof_seat
title: Tile the wall top smooth except a few jumper studs so a separately built roof locates on them and lifts off; use whenever the interior should be reachable.
why: Lets a roof or upper floor lift off to show the inside, which every house in the books does; pairs with wall_top_tie.

name: lift_off_floor
title: Lift-off upper floor made of two crossed layers of large plates around a stairwell opening, for every modular story.
why: Upper floors as their own units: two layers of plates with crossing seams around a stair opening. For any building of more than one story.

name: jettied_floor
title: Upper floor plate that projects one stud past the wall below on the street sides, for overhanging Tudor stories.
why: An upper story that overhangs the one below by a stud: an easy way to make a town house look old and real.

name: masonry_wall
title: Running-bond wall panel of embossed and plain bricks built flat and attached, for exposed brick, rear walls and chimneys.
why: Brick-textured walls in running bond with a few patched bricks; a plain wall made to read as brickwork.

name: clapboard_siding
title: A sideways siding strip of cheese slopes on a long plate, hung on side studs to give a wall or narrow pier lap-siding in another color.
why: Lap siding from slopes on a plate hung on side studs, for wooden houses and barns.

name: half_timber_band
title: White plaster wall with black timber posts and diagonal braces built studs-out, for Tudor or half-timbered upper stories.
why: White plaster with black timber posts and braces, for Tudor and half-timbered stories.

name: window_sill
title: A deep window sill from a flat 1x4 panel, with a two-stud plate on the base's side studs as a band below it.
why: A deep sill under a window, so windows don't sit flat in the wall.

name: window_hood
title: Small peaked hood over a window from two mirrored slopes on a plate, for upper-floor window trim.
why: A small peaked or flat hood over a window; with window_sill it frames a window the way the books do.

name: shuttered_window
title: An arched lattice window in a wall gap with shutter mounts on side studs either side; use for cottages and chapels.
why: A cottage window with shutters on side studs either side.

name: shop_window
title: Shop window on a 1x6 plate with small transom frames over taller panes and a bar course between, for ground-floor shopfronts.
why: A ground-floor shop window built as a unit on a plate, transoms over tall panes; for stations and town buildings.

name: door_hood
title: Cornice over a door from a 1x6 plate with corner plates and jumpers below and a tile on top, overhanging by one stud.
why: A projecting cornice over a door, held by jumpers and corner plates.

name: roof_dormer
title: A 45-degree pitched roof with a crossing front gable, a valley filler on a side stud and a rounded ridge; use for houses.
why: A small gable crossing a pitched roof, with the valley filled on a side stud; it breaks up a long roof.

name: ridge_cap
title: A row of curved-top bricks along a roof's ridge, so the ridge reads as a rounded roll.
why: A rounded cap along the ridge of a roof instead of a row of bare double slopes.

name: chimney_stack
title: Freestanding embossed-brick chimney with a stepped-out cap and round chimney pots, for rooftops.
why: A brick chimney with a stepped-out cap and pots, built on the roof.

name: downpipe
title: Rainwater downpipe of round 1x1 bricks stacked on a round plate up a wall corner.
why: A rainwater downpipe of round bricks up a wall corner; a cheap detail that makes a wall look finished.

name: porch_posts
title: Porch posts of a round 1x1 under a 1x1x3 brick, plus a balustrade of short spindles on studs capped with a tile rail.
why: Porch posts and a low balustrade, for porches, verandas, and station canopies.

name: sidewalk
title: Street edge of a modular baseplate: light tile curb, dark tile pavement and a few exposed studs for street furniture.
why: The street edge: a light tile curb and dark pavement with a few studs for street furniture.

name: wall_vent
title: A grille tile on the side studs of a 1x2 brick to make a vent, radiator or grate in a wall course.
why: A grille on the side studs of a brick in a wall course: a vent, radiator, or grate.
